$comment: GH-677 (queue item 6a) - THE GRAPH'S DEVICE FILLED IN FROM THE TEST'S OWN OUTPUT.
`runner` and `handle` are measured from the call sites, never from the plan's
tables: the cascade's run loop in `cascade-orchestrator.js` and the two pass
bodies in `hub-orchestrator.js` say which pass runs a module and through which
function. `requires` and `uses` are a JUDGEMENT about what the module does
without the input -- not compute at all, or compute differently -- and each is
filled from the reads the test prints, one line at a time.
`runner` AND `handle` ARE A LIST WHEN TWO PASSES RUN THE SAME MODULE. Four do:
shade, salinity penalty, wear recovery and stress trajectory each have a cascade
executor and an orchestrator builder, and both read inputs. A single string
would have to drop one of them, and the dropped one's reads would go unchecked.
The two lists are pairwise and the test holds their lengths equal.
A HANDLE MAY BE QUALIFIED `file:function` WHEN THE BARE NAME IS NOT UNIQUE.
`generateForecast` is declared in THREE files -- `disease-forecast.js`, `pgr-forecast.js` and `shade-forecast.js` --
and a bare name would silently resolve to whichever file came first -- the class
of silent first match this repository has spent the day removing. The test
reddens on an ambiguous bare name instead of choosing.
A NODE NO PASS RUNS KEEPS `runner: null` AND SAYS WHY, in `noRunnerBecause`.
Five do. Inventing a runner for them would put a module in the run that is not
in it; leaving the field empty without a reason would be indistinguishable from
work not yet done.
`_inputsBeforeTheSplit` is the old `inputs` list, carried over as the starting
point for the hand split and read by nothing.

GH-681: the cascade's executors are QUALIFIED with their file. Two places used to declare the cascade's engine list by hand -- `CASCADE_CONFIG.engineMap` and `GAIP_CASCADE_ENGINES` -- and deriving them from this data needs the data to say which handles belong to the cascade adapter. The bare name did not say it, and guessing by the `execute` prefix would be a rule about spelling rather than a fact about the file.

confidence.label: Analysis Confidence Summary
confidence.labelFrom: GH-777 (queue item 4, slice 2): the words a person reads for this step are the panel's (`STEP_NAMES['confidence']` = `Analysis confidence`), and GH-572's rule is that the panel takes its words FROM the node's label -- so the label has to carry them. `Engine Confidence Summary` was my own wording and would have made the module the one exception to that rule.
confidence.pageIsIntent: DECLARED INTENT, and it is a SECOND caller rather than a second producer. `assets/confidence-ui-integration.js:64` asks for the summary to decorate what is already on the screen, and that file is loaded by these five views -- which is why the walk finds the pair on each of them. The pass is what PRODUCES `computed.confidence`; the page's call writes nothing and stores nothing. Measured for GH-777: `getConfidenceSummary` has exactly two callers in `assets`, this decorator and the pass.
confidence.measured: GH-777 (queue item 4, slice 2) - A MEMBER OF THE PASS THAT THE GRAPH DID NOT KNOW. The pass has called this last since v1.3.0 (`hub-orchestrator.js`, `attempting("confidence")` then `GilbaEngineConfidence.getConfidenceSummary(_hubState)`), and its result is in 14 of 14 rows since 25.09 as `computed.confidence` - while the graph said nothing about it. The walk that replaces the pass's eleven hand-written gates reads THIS file to know who runs, so a member with no node would have lost its account of itself the day the walk arrived. `runner` and `handle` come from that call site, the output from the stored rows. `after` is every other node of the pass, because the summary reads the whole state the pass has built and can only be last. `requires` is empty on purpose: a summary of what the other engines did needs no input of the client's, and its absence is a module that failed to load rather than a site that is not a case for it.
confidence.sightBoundary: `assets/gilba-hub-v2.js:1546` installs a STUB `GilbaEngineConfidence` when the real module did not load, and the stub answers `wrapEngineOutput` only. So `getConfidenceSummary` is absent rather than wrong in that case, the pass produces no summary, and the end-of-pass sweep names it - which is the truth: nothing was computed. Measured, not reasoned: the stub carries no `getConfidenceSummary` key.

climate-engine.label: Climate Engine
climate-engine.runnerWidenedBecause: the caller fixpoint reaches it from the cascade as well, through the shade engine's handle, which both passes run. Declared narrow before GH-678 because the runner was decided by FILE.
climate-engine.pairwiseNoteGH678: RUNNER AND HANDLE ARE NOT PAIRWISE HERE, and the earlier rule that they must be is superseded rather than bent. Two passes run this module through ONE function, so a second handle would have to be invented -- I duplicated it once to satisfy the rule and that is a lie written as data. The rule that holds is: every handle resolves to a function, and the set of declared runners equals the set the caller fixpoint finds. Pairwise was a special case of that, not a law.

soil-temp-physics.label: Soil Temperature
soil-temp-physics.sightBoundary: UNIVERSE (c) IS BLIND TO THIS NODE, and that is said here rather than shown as a clean result. `enhancedSoilTemperature(airTemps, solarRadiation, soilMoisture, soilConfig)` takes SCALARS, not a state object, so the receiver sign -- the first parameter -- has no `<section>.<field>` to find and reports zero reads. Its inputs are assembled by the orchestrator inside `populateCanonicalState`; moving that call into the pass proper is queue item 3az.

ambient-dli-engine.label: Ambient DLI Engine
ambient-dli-engine.outputWasCalled: GH-777 (queue item 4, slice 2) - `computed.ambientDLI`, A ROW KEY NOBODY WRITES. Measured: absent from all 14 stored rows since 25.09, and no writer exists in either pass. What the engine's number actually does is go INTO another engine's input -- the pass calls it inside `buildShadeInputs` (`hub-orchestrator.js:3201`) and puts the value in `shadeState.turf.ambientDLI`, and where it reaches the row is `computed.shade.modular.ambientDLI`, written by the shade engine. So the node has no output of its own, and saying otherwise is what would have broken the pass: the walk of this slice registers a node as something the run must produce, and this one would have been reported as produced-nothing on every site -- 13 of 13 turning partial and a client reading `Ambient DLI was not calculated`. `derived.*` is the graph's own word for work that is not a row key -- `climate-engine` declares `derived.growthPotential` the same way -- and it is what the shade engine reads as `ambientDLI.current`. The node keeps its runners and its handle: both passes do reach it.
ambient-dli-engine.runnerWidenedBecause: reached from both passes through the shade builder. Its `page` pairs are divergences under GH-680, not intent.
ambient-dli-engine.pairwiseNoteGH678: RUNNER AND HANDLE ARE NOT PAIRWISE HERE, and the earlier rule that they must be is superseded rather than bent. Two passes run this module through ONE function, so a second handle would have to be invented -- I duplicated it once to satisfy the rule and that is a lie written as data. The rule that holds is: every handle resolves to a function, and the set of declared runners equals the set the caller fixpoint finds. Pairwise was a special case of that, not a law.

readsWithNoPlaceInTheList.why: Read here with a substitution, and NO surface fills them -- not a form, not the wizard, not the API (measured 24.09.2026 over `app/resources/views`, `assets` and `app`). They are left UNDECLARED on purpose: where an input with no place belongs in the list is the analyst's decision, and until it is made declaring them here would either break the list's own guards or claim a place that does not exist. `fertility.monthlyN` is the measured cost of the question: 37 of 37 stored rows carry the nitrogen engine's skipped stub because nothing fills it.

wear-recovery-engine.label: Wear & Recovery Engine
$comment: GH-787 (queue item 3vy) - ONE RUNNER, ONE HANDLE, ONE OUTPUT KEY.
This node declared two runners and two handles, and that was not redundancy: each runner built the
engine's inputs its own way, so one calculation had two answers. Measured on the stand across the last
row of every site - the two disagreed about the recovery window at 10 of 10 sites (Test5 - NZ 17 days
against 7, Russley 28 against 12), about the recovery probability at 9, and about the species and the
variety they were given at all 10. The client is shown the orchestrator's figure; the cascade's went
into the row beside it under `computed.wearRecovery`.
The cascade stopped calling it because this list is what it walks (`gaip_cascadeEnginesFromTheGraph`).
`computed.wearRecovery` and `derived.adjustedRecoveryDays` left the outputs with the code that wrote
them: the alias had no reader on any client page, and the second stress pass it stood for was removed
by the owner's decision of 30.09.2026 - stress enters the recovery days once, inside the engine.
`uses` NAMES THE PATHS THE ASSEMBLY ACTUALLY READS, and since this item they are the paths the value is
STORED at rather than the names the page's state used: `turf.hoc` where it said `turf.heightOfCut`,
`traffic.schedule.rootDepth` and `traffic.schedule.moisture` where the form supplied them, plus
`turf.species` -- which the assembly used to take from the canonical state of the PAGE, five sources deep.

`site.construction` is gone with the `|| "native"` chain that read it, and the two inputs the form used to supply are named by their KEY in the inputs list (`soil.moisture`, `turf.rootDepth`) while the assembly reads them at the path that list declares they are stored at.

GH-790 (queue item 9) - THE LOAD COMES FROM THE SITE'S OWN SCHEDULE, so the input's name changes with its source. `schedule.traffic` was `_hubState.inputs.schedule`, which no writer in the product ever fills -- so this engine was handed no load on any run, while the cascade built one out of fifteen fields of the `/hub` markup. Both paths now take `traffic.schedule` of the config of the site the run is for, through one transform, and GH-776's rule travels inside it: a site that is not a sports field, and a sports field with no schedule, carry no traffic.

irrigation-scheduler.label: Irrigation Scheduler
irrigation-scheduler.noRunnerBecause: GH-755 (queue item 3bz) removed `executeEngine`, which held the ONLY call site of this node's handle -- measured on the bench: zero call sites outside that export. THE PASS DOES NOT COMPUTE IRRIGATION AND NO STORED ROW CARRIES `computed.irrigation`: measured by JSON type over all 80 rows, the key holds JSON null in 77 and is absent in 3, an object in none. Irrigation is computed by the /hub rendering instead -- `hub-tissue-v3.js` sets `window.GAIP_IRRIGATION_RESULT` -- and reaches a row from there through `hub-persistence.js` as `metrics.irrigationNeed` and `computed.waterBalance.weeklyNeed`, a number in 76 of 80 rows each. THE NODE STAYS ON ONE THING, AND IT IS DECLARED, NOT MEASURED: both forecast nodes name it in their `after`. Neither of those two runs either -- `irrigation-forecast` also has `runner: null` and an empty `uses` -- and whether the forecast drawn on the page reads this schedule has not been measured. Whether the irrigation schedule should run inside the pass is a product question and belongs to the owner.

pgr-module.label: PGR Module
pgr-module.noRunnerBecause: GH-755 (queue item 3bz) removed `executeEngine`, which held the ONLY call site of this node's handle and the only writes of `computed.pgr` -- measured on the bench: zero call sites outside that export, zero entries in 6987. THE NODE STAYS for two reasons, both measured: `computed.pgr` IS in the stored rows -- by JSON type, an object in 13 of 80 rows, all of them one site (`Russley`) -- and both forecast nodes name this node in their `after`. Whether PGR should run inside the pass is a product question and belongs to the owner.

water-blender.label: Water Quality
water-blender.labelWasCalled: Water Blender until GH-677. The label is the word a CLIENT reads -- it is the subject of "{Module} was not calculated..." -- and the panel already says "water quality" for this module (`AnalysisNotice::STEP_NAMES`). Two words for one module, one of them internal; this takes the one already on the screen rather than inventing a third.

scenario-engine.label: Scenario Comparison
scenario-engine.labelFrom: the label is the subject of "{Module} was not calculated...", so it is a word the client already reads. Taken from the page rather than written here: "Scenario Comparison" is the heading of `reports/scenarios.blade.php`.
scenario-engine.pageIsIntent: DECLARED INTENT. The engine declares globals and does not start itself; `gaip-whatif-ui.js` calls it on a human action, and that file is loaded by `hub` and `reports/scenarios`. The intent is the scenarios page.
scenario-engine.handleWasWrong: assets/gaip-scenario-engine.js:buildState until the caller fixpoint said `declared page never calls it`. `buildState` is an internal step; the entry a human reaches is `GAIP_ScenarioEngine.compareScenarios`, which `gaip-whatif-ui.js` names as its primary call (its own comment at line 861), with `runScenario` as the other. The handle has to be the function somebody actually enters the module by.

disease-forecast.label: Disease Forecast
disease-forecast.outputWasCalled: computed.diseaseForecast until GH-677. No pass ever wrote that key; the pass writes `computed.forecast` from `DiseaseForecast.generateForecast`. The node was not missing, its output was misnamed -- which is why (a) printed it on both sides at once.

irrigation-forecast.noRunnerBecause: No pass writes `computed.irrigationForecast`; the orchestrator says in place of a call "Irrigation scheduler would be called here". It renders on a page. Waits for 3ayu.
